summary: Over 14 days with 98.7% CGM coverage, mean glucose was 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0%, and time below range 5.1%. Local 00:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00 carried most hypoglycemia, while local 14:00-17:00 carried most hyperglycemia. The selected profile is complete and declared applicable, but carbs were not logged, so UAM and SMB ran the meal path. Competing basal, target, residual IOB, DynISF, and SMB explanations are not separated, so this synthesis keeps every current profile and AAPS value and sequences verification before any later review.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM quality supports time-of-day review: 3995 valid entries, 0 invalid, about 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes. The selected AAPS profile is complete. Therapy context is incomplete because carb entries are 0 g, representative treatments are a slice of 2315 treatments, and a profile switch plus site, sensor, GLP-1, and pump events break a single-cause read of the whole fortnight.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits later review: TBR 5.1% with clusters at local 00:00-03:00 (hour 1 TBR 18.5%) and local 18:00-19:00 (hour 19 TBR 15.3%), including 41-42 mg/dL extremes. Afternoon TAR peaks at local hour 16 (32.1%). Sampled IOB reached about 4.7-5.9 U against about 19.7 U per day mean insulin, so max IOB 25 U was not the binding brake. Overnight insulin must not be increased, and the 90 mg/dL overnight target must not be tightened, until residual IOB is separated from basal and target.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal is about 16.2 U/day if fully delivered. Local 05:00-08:00 is the most stable fasting-like window. Local 00:00-03:00 lows sit on 0.6 U/h basal and a 90 mg/dL target but also on evening IOB. The 16:00 drop to 0.5 U/h coincides with the worst TAR hour and is followed by evening crashes, so it is not a clean basal deficit. The 08:00 target 100 mg/dL overlaps breakfast-like rises. These patterns are not labeled as isolated basal defects.

analysis_steps.findings: Five CR segments exist but had no carb entries to act on, so CR is untestable. Flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U is already overwritten in loop samples by DynISF (variable_sens about 28-124). Correction windows show both late rises after tiny insulin and 2-4 hour undershoots, which are meal-contaminated. DIA 10 h can leave evening insulin active overnight. No CR, ISF, or DIA number is isolated enough to change.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are on with always-on SMB, which matches COB 0 and unused CR. High temporary targets should suppress SMB and were used as a brake. Delivery is 3-minute SMB interval, 15-minute SMB cap, 20-minute UAM cap; enacted reasons still show UAM boosts and SMBs larger than nominal basal-minute math. Overnight samples often stop on minGuardBG, so 00:00-03:00 TBR is not proven live overnight SMB. Afternoon catch-up then evening crash remains the stronger UAM story.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is declared off; a sensitivity_ratio of 1 is only a neutral sample, not proof of Autosens state. DynISF on at 70% is the live sensitivity lever and can explain strong effective ISF at high glucose. max_basal 12 U/h is looser than the about 4 U/h maxSafeBasal already seen. max_iob 25 U never bound observed IOB near 6 U. Carb-absorption 8 mg/dL/5 min and 7 h were idle with 0 g carbs. Automation is compensating for unlogged meals and flat ISF and may also create overshoot; that is not a license to change DynISF, ISF, and SMB together.

Observed execution is correction insulin plus UAM/SMB, not announced meal boluses. Windows show late rises after small insulin and later undershoots when more insulin stacked. No immediate-bolus percent can be calculated without inventing grams or a bolus split.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked explanation for afternoon highs then evening and overnight lows: unannounced intake handled late by always-on UAM/SMB, DynISF stronger at peaks, then DIA 10 h residual IOB into target 90 mg/dL. Alternate explanations (00:00 basal 0.6 U/h too high, 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h too low, 19:00 basal 0.7 U/h too high, CR too weak, ISF 56 too strong by itself) remain possible and were not separated. Package overrides any earlier impulse to edit a single row: historical_applicability is yes for the selected profile, but the 08-13 switch, GLP-1 notes, and 08-19 occlusion lower causal confidence. Conservative sequence is keep every current value, verify overnight lows against evening IOB first, then review only one automation family if needed, and only then consider CR or e-carbs after carbs are logged.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined glucose time-of-day tables, zero carb telemetry, selected aaps_profile values, loop IOB and variable_sens, empty declared meal strategy, decision_inventory complete current values.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The single most useful missing observation is meal start time and grams on usual daytime intakes, plus evening IOB on nights with 00:00-03:00 lows.

strengths: CGM coverage is 98.7% with a regular 5-minute cadence, which is enough for time-of-day pattern review.
Overall time in range is 86.0% with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL.
Local 05:00-08:00 is consistently flat and in range, so the dawn basal step is not an obvious under-delivery window.
The selected profile is complete across basal, CR, ISF, targets, DIA, and the six AAPS groups.
High temporary targets at 135 mg/dL were already used as a protective brake on some high-risk windows.
Closed loop remained the observed mode, and overnight samples often halted dosing on low minGuardBG rather than blindly adding SMB.
issues: Time below range is 5.1%, clustered at local 00:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00, with extremes near 41-42 mg/dL.
Afternoon time above range is concentrated at local 14:00-17:00 and is often followed by a late crash rather than a stable landing.
Coefficient of variation is 32.6%, so the mean and time-in-range hide a high-then-low swing.
Zero carb entries make CR, prebolus, immediate bolus percent, and e-carbs untestable; UAM/SMB is the observed meal controller.
Sampled IOB of about 5-6 U shows stacking is possible well below max IOB 25 U.
An 08-13 profile switch, GLP-1 notes, site and sensor changes, and an 08-19 occlusion/pump error confound any single-parameter story.

recommendations.title: Keep overnight target and basal; verify residual IOB first
recommendations.description: Local midnight lows sit on a 90 mg/dL target and 0.6 U/h basal, but they also follow afternoon UAM/SMB stacks, DynISF at high glucose, and a 10 h DIA. Those causes are not separated, so no overnight insulin increase and no tighter overnight target are supported. The first safe action is observation, not a profile edit.

suggested_change.direction: Retain 90 mg/dL overnight targets and 0.6 U/h from 00:00. Compare local 00:00-03:00 glucose on nights with low evening IOB versus nights after a large afternoon UAM or correction stack.

recommendations.title: Review only one automation family after overnight verification
recommendations.description: If low-IOB nights are fine and the remaining problem is still a late rise then crash, the next review family is automation (DynISF factor or SMB/UAM delivery), not CR and not a simultaneous ISF change. Changing those together would hide which lever mattered.

suggested_change.direction: Leave DynISF 70%, SMB interval 3 min, UAM 20 min, and ISF 56 mg/dL/U unchanged until overnight IOB verification is done. If a later review is still needed, discuss only one of those families.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current 90 mg/dL overnight target and every other basal, CR, ISF, and DIA row. Use the next check to see whether local 00:00-03:00 lows persist when evening IOB is low.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The only profile rows that touch the main safety cluster are overnight target 90 mg/dL and overnight basal 0.6 U/h. Afternoon TAR and evening crashes can equally be unlogged meals plus UAM and DynISF. Package evidence does not isolate a safe old-to-new profile number, and historical_applicability of the selected profile does not remove the 08-13 switch or GLP-1 confounding.
profile_recommendation.next_check: On at least several nights, note evening IOB around local 21:00-23:00 and whether local 00:00-03:00 still goes below range when that IOB is low and no late correction was given.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local 00:00-03:00 TBR is high, but sampled nights also carry residual IOB and a 90 mg/dL target. Uncertainty: basal versus IOB versus target is unresolved. Dependencies: safety veto on adding overnight insulin; DIA 10 h and afternoon UAM stacks. A change is unsupported.
Evidence: local 05:00-07:00 means are near 99-104 mg/dL with TIR about 95-99%. Uncertainty: low for a defect in this row. Dependencies: later 08:00-10:00 rise is meal-timed. No isolated basal change.
Evidence: local 06:00-08:00 remains in range before the breakfast-like climb. Uncertainty: cannot split dawn basal from the 08:00 target 100 mg/dL. Dependencies: meal and UAM lag after 08:00. Keep.

Evidence: late-morning and midday TAR exists, but several windows rise after tiny correction insulin and COB 0, which fits unlogged intake. Uncertainty: high that this basal row is the cause. Dependencies: UAM delay, unused CR, GLP-1 notes. Keep.

Evidence: this is the lowest daytime basal under the worst TAR hour, yet local 18:00-19:00 TBR is also the worst evening hypo cluster. Uncertainty: the 0.5 U/h row may already be compensating for crashes. Dependencies: UAM/SMB and DynISF still open. Raising it is unsupported.

Evidence: glucose is already falling through local 18:00-19:00 after afternoon stacks. Uncertainty: basal versus residual insulin is not separated. Dependencies: hour-19 TBR, DIA, user corrections. Keep.

Evidence: 0.7 U/h starts as local hour 19 TBR reaches 15.3%, but that hour includes 41 mg/dL extremes after prior UAM and corrections. Uncertainty: this row is a weaker explanation than residual IOB. Dependencies: 16:00 basal, SMB/UAM, DynISF. Keep.

Evidence: carb_entries 0 and loop COB 0, so this CR never ran. Uncertainty: complete for meal effect. Dependencies: empty declared meal strategy and always-on UAM. Changing CR would not explain this dataset.
Evidence: no carb treatments in this or any segment. Uncertainty: untestable. Dependencies: unused carb-absorption settings. Keep.
Evidence: local 08:00-10:00 rise occurs with COB 0, so UAM, not this CR, dosed any meal. Uncertainty: high for any CR number. Dependencies: meal logging absent. Keep.
Evidence: the tightest CR sits under the afternoon TAR window but had no grams to apply. Uncertainty: unused. Dependencies: UAM/SMB and DynISF explain more of the observed insulin. Keep.
Evidence: evening crashes follow already-delivered insulin, not announced dinner carbs. Uncertainty: CR unused. Dependencies: DIA tail and overnight target. Keep.

Evidence: flat 56 mg/dL/U while DynISF 70% already moved variable_sens from about 28 to above 100; correction windows are meal-contaminated. Uncertainty: profile ISF versus DynISF versus SMB stack is unresolved. Dependencies: do not change ISF with DynISF or SMB delivery. Keep.

Evidence: overnight target 90 mg/dL sits under the largest TBR cluster, but residual IOB is an equally strong cause. Uncertainty: medium-high. Dependencies: 23:00 target return to 90, DIA 10 h, evening automation. Tightening is unsafe; raising is still a correlated guess, so keep and verify.
Evidence: daytime target 100 mg/dL overlaps a meal-like rise, not a fasting overshoot. Uncertainty: target versus breakfast-timed UAM. Dependencies: unused CR. Keep.

Evidence: target returns to 90 mg/dL just before the midnight dip. Uncertainty: same residual-IOB confound as the 00:00 target. Dependencies: evening stacks and 00:00 basal. Keep pending the overnight IOB check.

Evidence: long DIA can keep afternoon insulin active at night and also restrain some dosing; observed UAM still built 5-6 U IOB. Uncertainty: high without peak-model and meal-time detail, including any dilute-insulin context. Dependencies: IOB accounting, SMB/UAM, overnight lows. Keep.

Evidence: with 0 g carbs, SMB and UAM are the only meal controller and match declared empty meal_strategies. Uncertainty: they also likely contribute to evening IOB. Dependencies: activation and delivery groups; turning them off without carb logging has no tested alternative. Keep.

Evidence: always-on SMB is internally consistent with unused COB switches; high TT false is consistent with 135 mg/dL temporary targets used as a brake. Uncertainty: always-on remains an amplifier when no TT is set. Dependencies: meal logging still absent. A change is unsupported until carbs are announced. Keep.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: observed IOB near 6 U never approached 25 U, and enacted temps were already clipped near 4 U/h by multipliers, not by the 12 U/h cap. Uncertainty: lowering max IOB would not have blocked the recorded hypos. Dependencies: SMB/DynISF aggressiveness. Keep rather than invent a new unused ceiling.

Evidence: Autosens is off and its target flags are unused; DynISF 70% is the active compensator for flat ISF 56 and a leading overshoot candidate. Uncertainty: GLP-1 and unlogged meals still confound. Dependencies: profile ISF and SMB delivery. Enabling Autosens or changing the 70% factor together with ISF is unsupported. Keep.
Evidence: no carb entries, so these settings had no operational effect and do not explain UAM or TBR. Uncertainty: none for this period's dosing path. Dependencies: future carb logging only. Keep.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: There is no declared prebolus time, no declared immediate bolus percent, and no e-carb plan; observed meals were handled by always-on SMB and UAM with COB 0. Keep that combination explicit rather than inventing a prebolus or percent. If carbs begin to be entered, announce them so CR can be tested, treat UAM as backup rather than a second full meal dose, and leave e-carbs off until a logged slow-absorption pattern exists.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Declared meal_strategies is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null, which is an absent declaration, not a Nightscout failure to confirm a filled field. Telemetry shows late rises after small corrections and 2-4 hour undershoots when insulin stacked, fitting UAM-only timing plus DynISF and a 10 h DIA into evening and overnight hypo risk.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record start clock time and grams for several usual daytime intakes, especially on GLP-1 days, and pair those notes with evening IOB.

exceptions.pattern: Local 14:00-17:00 already high or rising with active IOB
exceptions.suggestion: Avoid stacking extra correction boluses on top of UAM in that window; a high temporary target was the observed alternative in this period.
exceptions.rationale: Several correction windows fell from the 170-230s into the 40-60s within 2-4 hours.

exceptions.pattern: Late-morning or midday delayed rise with almost no announced insulin
exceptions.suggestion: This pattern is late delivery, not a proven weak CR; logging start time matters more than adding e-carbs.
exceptions.rationale: Repeated 100-140 to 160-235 mg/dL climbs occurred with 0 g carbs and tiny listed corrections.

implementation_steps: Treat this output as decision-support for discussion only. Independently verify each number against the pump and AAPS screens before any review.
Confirm that the selected profile in this package is the profile still in use, and remember the 08-13 switch so pre-switch days are not used as a clean test of the current rows.
Keep all current basal, target, CR, ISF, and DIA values. First observe local 00:00-03:00 glucose against evening IOB and late corrections.
Do not raise overnight basal or tighten the 90 mg/dL overnight target during that watch.
If low-IOB nights are still low, discuss overnight target or basal only as a later single-family review, not together with SMB or DynISF.
If low-IOB nights are fine and the remaining pattern is afternoon rise then evening crash, review only one automation family (DynISF factor or SMB/UAM delivery), not both, and not with profile ISF.
Leave CR, carb-absorption, and e-carb fields unchanged until meal start times and grams are logged.
Make at most one discussed change at a time, watch several days including the known hypo clocks, and account for GLP-1 notes, site changes, and pump alerts before judging the result.
education: Time below range near 5% with clock-clustered lows is a safety pattern even when overall time in range is high.
UAM is not the same as entering carbs and is not automatic duplicate COB; in this file COB stayed 0, so UAM was the meal path.
A sensitivity_ratio of 1 in a loop sample is a neutral current adjustment, not evidence that Autosens is on. Autosens is declared off here while DynISF is on.
DIA 10 h means afternoon insulin can still be counted at midnight, which can look like an overnight basal problem when it is leftover IOB.
E-carbs are a carb-absorption announcement, not a pump extended bolus, and none were present to interpret.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. It is not medical advice and it does not change AAPS.
Independently verify every proposed review, discuss changes with the care team, make at most one change at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Documented lows reached about 41-42 mg/dL. Do not increase overnight insulin or tighten the 90 mg/dL overnight target while residual IOB remains a plausible cause.
Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h did not constrain the observed stacks; large IOB still appeared after occlusion catch-up and high-BG UAM.
GLP-1 notes, site and sensor changes, and the 08-19 occlusion and pump error can mimic a profile error.
